subject: english-language
title: Two Words and Telegrams
welcome_lead: Grammar arrives. Watch two-word combinations bloom and telegraphic speech compress meaning to its core.
meta_desc: Two-word stage, telegraphic speech and pivot grammars in child language acquisition at A-Level.
final_note: You have witnessed grammar emerging — pivots, semantic relations and the first telegrams of thought.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Around 18 months children combine two words. Braine observed many followed a pivot + open pattern: a small set of high-frequency words (more, allgone) combined with content words.

Brown's semantic relations capture the meanings expressed: agent-action (baby fall), possession (mummy shoe).

By 24-30 months utterances grow to 3-4 words but function morphemes are still scarce: daddy go work, doggy eat bone.

Brown (1973) traced the order in which grammatical morphemes are mastered — present progressive -ing first, then plural -s, then irregular past.
Brown's MLU counts morphemes per utterance averaged over a sample. He proposed five stages, with MLU moving from 1.0 (one-word) toward 4.0+ as complex syntax emerges.

mcqs.q: What is the telegraphic stage of child language development?
options: Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
It is the stage when children first start using a telephone.
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Around age 2-3, children produce short utterances containing content words but omitting function words and inflections (e.g. 'mummy gone shop').

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.

mcqs.q: How does Piaget's theory relate language to cognitive development?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Piaget said language drives cognitive development.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.

Language develops as a consequence of cognitive development — children must first develop concepts (object permanence, conservation) before they can express them linguistically. Cognition leads language.
